title: Kathy Castor criticizes Trump policies and promotes children's health care act
text:
Congresswoman Kathy Castor | Official U.S. House headshot
Congresswoman Kathy Castor | Official U.S. House headshot
U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor, who represents Florida’s 14th district in Congress, recently addressed issues related to economic policy and children’s health care coverage through a series of posts on her social media account.
On August 12, 2025, Castor criticized former President Donald Trump for policies she claims negatively impact American families. She stated, "Trump is raising your grocery bill to line the wallets of his billionaire friends. Nothing great about this for American families across the country."
The following day, August 13, 2025, Castor advocated for uninterrupted health care coverage for children and promoted her legislative initiative. She wrote, "Our children’s access to health care should not be on the chopping block to pay for tax breaks for billionaires.
My Keeping Kids Covered Act would ensure protection for uninterrupted coverage for children until age 6, because no matter who is in power, our kids deserve to be".
Later that same day, Castor posted an enthusiastic message without additional context: "WOOOOOOOO ".
Castor has served as a member of the U.S. Congress since 2007 after replacing Jim Davis and previously held office in the Florida House of Representatives. Born in Miami in 1966 and currently residing in Tampa at age 56, she holds degrees from Emory University (BA) and Florida State University (JD).
